_what: The Mariano's published site taxonomy and SEO product list, read from the retailer's own sitemap. Observed values only: every slug and id below is copied from a sitemap URL. Nothing here is inferred, and nothing here is store-specific - a sitemap is site-wide, so it says what categories and pages exist, not what the Vernon Hills store carries or what anything costs.
captured_how: Read in a browser on an ordinary residential connection, one GET per sitemap file, five files in total. A curl of the same URL from a datacenter egress was refused with an HTTP/2 INTERNAL_ERROR before any HTTP exchange, which is the same refusal shape measured from two Azure regions on 30 October. No bot challenge was answered and none was bypassed.

robots_txt.note: robots.txt does not disallow /pl/ listing pages, /p/ product pages or /search, and it advertises the sitemap that was read here. Store location lookups are disallowed, which is why the store is resolved through Kroger's documented Locations API instead.

_id_structure: A listing id encodes its own depth: 2 digits is a department, 5 digits is that department plus a 3-digit subcategory, 10 digits is that plus a 5-digit leaf. So 60 is asian-food, 60004 is asian-appetizers inside it, 6000400001 is a leaf inside that.

seo_product_pages._caution: This is the retailer's SEO product list, not its catalogue. 890 URLs against 26,166 products already collected from the API at one store means the product sitemap is a curated subset and is NOT a route to complete product enumeration. It is useful only as an independently published sample to test our own coverage against.
